_comment: What each tool's decoder needs on the device, for the trade-off graph (plot.py). ram is bytes of RAM while patching; with plus_old_file, the decoder also holds the whole old file (the dictionary) in RAM, so the graph adds the median old-file size of each kind of data and marks the point as a lower bound. code is .text in bytes, null where no microcontroller build exists. basis says where each number comes from: measured (bench/decoder-size.sh, Cortex-M0, -Os) or the tool's documentation.

tinydelta_optimal.label: tinydelta
tinydelta_optimal.basis: measured: callback decoder, Cortex-M0, -Os: 670 B code with arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2 (712 B with 10.3, as in the README), ~200 B of stack, no static RAM

tinydelta_zlib.label: tinydelta + zlib
tinydelta_zlib.basis: tinydelta's ~200 B plus an inflate window of 32 KB: the patches are compressed with zlib's default 15-bit window

hpatchlite_4k.label: HPatchLite, 4 KB dict.
hpatchlite_4k.basis: HPatchLite README: one decompression dictionary plus an input cache of at least 3 B; stack and code from bench/decoder-size.sh

hpatchlite_32k.label: HPatchLite, 32 KB dict.
hpatchlite_32k.basis: as HPatchLite, 4 KB dict., with the default 32 KB dictionary

detools.label: detools (heatshrink)
detools.basis: measured with detools' default heatshrink settings, Cortex-M0: ~1.6 KB stack, 1,948 B code (README benchmark)

bsdiff.label: bsdiff
bsdiff.basis: bzip2 manual: decompressing 900 KB blocks needs about 3.7 MB, or 2.3 MB in small mode; bspatch also holds old and new file in memory

zstd.label: zstd --patch-from
zstd.basis: zstd --patch-from uses the whole old file as its window, so the decoder needs at least the old file in memory

openvcdiff.label: open-vcdiff
openvcdiff.basis: open-vcdiff's decoder (C++) works on the whole dictionary in memory

xdelta3.label: xdelta3
xdelta3.basis: xdelta3 keeps the source in memory in blocks (default 8 MB window), which covers the whole old file at these sizes
